pr_title: Made changes to optimize service collection lookups
pr_body:
- Added concrete Try* methods to the ServiceCollection
- Added tests for more operations to ensure consistency
- Kept the methods internal since they don't need to be public for this optimization

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/44728

TODO: Run some performance tests

cc @benaadams

issue_context.title: Optimize ServiceCollectionDescriptorExtensions TryAdd
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @eerhardt, @maryamariyan See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
Description: See the conversation here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/44696/files#r523781023 We are currently looping over the IServiceCollection looking if a ServiceDescriptor has already been added for this ServiceType. Not only are we going through the whole collection for each new service added, but we are also making interface dispatches for each element. Instead, we should introduce a new interface that [`ServiceCollection`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/162b33e19eb5a3434867541be691e1082039b130/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection/src/ServiceCollection.cs#L12) implements, so we can fast path this check. While introducing this new interface, we should analyze if there are other paths on the startup path that can be optimized as well, in case we need other new methods. cc @davidfowl @stephentoub @benaadams
Author: eerhardt
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-Extensions-DependencyInjection`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -

2. Consider ServiceCollection keeps implementing previous IList<> interface

Based on [conversation](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/44696/files#r523781023), should ServiceCollection add new Dictionary<ServiceType, collection of serviceDescriber> field and keep old List field? This will have synchronous action when calling modified related method for example RemoveAll() ? 
Or other solution ?
Thanks!

Outside of unit tests (where we probably don't really care about an inefficient fallback), there is one other third party implementation I am aware of:

Lamar implements IServiceCollection on its main Registry type. They even encourage users to skip the RegisterServices Method in Startup entirely, and just use ` public void ConfigureContainer(ServiceRegistry services)`, so you can freely mix service registrations based on IServiceCollection extension methods with native registrations that can use its additional features.

https://github.com/JasperFx/lamar/blob/3a4a744db889b582ae57f6e01c5fa5bdec765e30/src/Lamar/ServiceRegistry.cs#L39

On everything but netstandard2.0.

Yep. I'd wager that 98% of use cases are ServiceCollection instances. Though I don't have a problem trying to make this work for Lamar as well.

Right, I don't think there's an either or here. We should do the move and the cast anyways. We can use DIMs on IServiceCollection as well on .NET Core specific frameworks. I'm just saying that besides Lamar, I don't think anyone extends this type *and* it forces them to cross compile for the performance boost anyways. As long as that's fine, we can do both things.

@davidfowl I am one of those that implement their own IServiceCollection. It is not uncommon when creating non-MS DI integrations. My IServiceCollection wraps my DI's container's builder, to expose 'fake' service registrations out of it, so it 'looks like' services registered outside of MS DI are present.

Because so many MS libraries try to call TryAdd* and then duplicate crap if they don't see it already present.

Without this, I end up with a billion registrations of IOptions stuff, for instance.

If there were Try* methods available to me, I'd implement those directly on my IServiceCollection, instead of exposing a manufactured fake list of stuff.

review_comments:
This test shows how weird the Replace API works.

1. Start with: `[b]`
2. Insert `a` at the beginning: `[a, b]`
3. Replace with `c`: `[b, c]`

`a` got replaced, but `c` got added to the end. And `b` is still there.
Yea, I couldn't figure out why replace was so weird until I was re-implementing it.
I thought these were going to be public... That's why we took this to API review.
Yea, I know but now I'm not sure it needs to be unless we do the other thing (the base class).
If we just want to rely on the extension methods... I'm fine with that. But we should go back to the API issue and update it that we only moved the type and didn't add the APIs.

Base class doesn't solve any problems; the issue is if someone has the interface `IServiceCollection` on a class with an existing heirachy introducing a base class doesn't give you anything?

They can't now inherit from the base class as C# doesn't support multiple inheritance. (Which is where DIMs do work as they can override the DIM methods)

> We would rather add a base class and make people rebase that want these optimizations

Which is essentially forcing breaking changes on the implementors of the interface?

Also something like `Cysharp/MessagePipe` [`struct ContainerBuilderProxy : IServiceCollection`](https://github.com/Cysharp/MessagePipe/blob/master/src/MessagePipe.Unity/Assets/Plugins/MessagePipe.VContainer/Runtime/TypeProxy.cs) is a struct so can't inherit from a base class.

Just keeping to the dotnet org `dotnet/maui` already has serveral implementations of `IServiceCollection` and is exposing multiple derived `IServiceCollections` as part of its public api e.g. `IMauiServiceCollection` looks to be used as part of hot reload in some way https://github.com/dotnet/maui/pull/851

> Which is essentially forcing breaking changes on the implementors of the interface?

It's not a breaking change. The implementors can continue doing what they are doing today, they just don't get this optimization.

> something like Cysharp/MessagePipe struct ContainerBuilderProxy : IServiceCollection is a struct

Isn't that a bad idea because you are boxing every time you pass it into a method that takes `IServiceCollection`?
YEP 😄

Also I assume if you include a ns2.0 lib that has a transient dependency with a net6 vairant and use it in a net6 app it will use the net6 version? So not sure what the issue is there? 

Cross compiling `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions` with DIMs will just mean it doesn't have a fast path for the DIMs on Framework? Upgrade to .NET6+; a newer classic Mono or an [updated Unity](https://forum.unity.com/threads/unity-future-net-development-status.1092205/) and its will be good. Don't think its a probablem that only Framework doesn't have the option of a faster path with DIMs? 

They aren't taking anything away, can still rebase on `ServiceCollection` (and then have issues that can't override any of the methods to fit with custom changes). DIMs keep the implementation open, whereas base class closes routes of inhetience and doesn't ingetrate unless everything is virtual, but then that's not great either.

It would be less of an issue if `IServiceCollection` was new and no-one had implemented it but is been out there for 5 years, so saying everyone that implements `IServiceCollection` should inherit from `ServiceCollection` seems a bit much? Also kinda makes the interface pointless?
Don't have issues with this PR though :)

I think we should open a new issue about extensibility. This issue is about optimizing the 90% case. I'm not a fan of using DIMs in libraries that cross compile, it feels wrong to differ the contract based on runtime capabilities. That said, it's unrelated to optimizing this code path.

> > Which is essentially forcing breaking changes on the implementors of the interface?
> 
> It's not a breaking change. The implementors can continue doing what they are doing today, they just don't get this optimization.

Which is why I don't understand how adding some DIMs would be an issue? It wouldn't effect anyone that doesn't want to implement them (they'd still go via this path); while giving the option to optimize. However I don't see how a base class would add anything other than making all the methods virtual for everybody?

> I'm not a fan of using DIMs in libraries that cross compile, it feels wrong to differ the contract based on runtime capabilities.

It falls out as estension methods where no runtime support and overridable DIM methods for runtimes with support. 

Don't see how is much different than the System.Memory package offerring extensions for string etc to add `.AsSpan()/.AsMemory()` which exist as instance methods when the runtime has support.

Span and Memory aren't abstractions that you implement, that's why its different. I don't like the fact that contracts are different across TFMs, that's what feels wrong. Implementation, sure, not the contract
If we aren't going to make these APIs public, it is kind of pointless to have them return `bool` when no one consumes it.

When learn these code, just found here is a bug maybe?

Based on current implementation of 'Remove' related [methods](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/79c0e0417ad98ac6021303a1a11180c1be8012ab/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions/src/ServiceCollection.cs#L75), they are not removing empty collection for specific ServiceType from dictionary if there is only one item for that ServiceType before calling 'Remove()'. So when user calls TryAdd() here after calling Remove(), it will refuse to add requested item with previous ServiceType even if it is not existing actually.

Add serviceDescripter (TypeA) -> Remove (TypeA) -> TryAdd() (TypeA) (will fail)

If my understanding above is right, besides of fixing in current PR, maybe I can also have opportunity to create new PR to change it just after this is merged ? :)
That's a bug in the current PR, that should be fixed! Good catch!
